result: `GET /health` now runs a real database round trip on every probe. `config/health.ts` builds a `HealthManager` from `@guren/core`'s health subsystem, registering a `DatabaseCheck` (named `database`, `critical: true`, 3s timeout) over a small `DatabaseConnection` adapter that resolves `getDatabase()` per call and runs `SELECT 1` through Drizzle's `db.get(sql.raw(...))` — the handle is fetched on each probe, so a connection that cannot be opened fails the check rather than being masked by a cached one, and the check catches its own errors so a dead database can never escape as a 500. `app/Http/Controllers/HealthController.ts` renders the report as `{ status, timestamp, checks: [{ name: "database", status, message, durationMs }] }` and maps `healthy → 200`, anything else → `503`; `routes/web.ts` now points the (still unauthenticated, still host-authorization-exempt) `/health` route at `[HealthController, 'index']` with the name `health`, and `.guren/routes.gen.ts` / `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` were regenerated for that name. `tests/HealthController.test.ts` covers the healthy 200 body, that the probe queries on every call instead of caching a verdict, unhealthy on a throwing query and on one that never settles, and an end-to-end 503 by dropping the connection and repointing it at an unopenable path (restored afterwards). `bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` is green at 7/7; `bunx guren check` reports 10 passed with only the pre-existing missing-test warnings.
